# Libya’s fragile transition plagued by deepening economic and political divides 

 

 © UN Photo/Abel Kavangh A view of Tripoli, Libya. 

# Libya’s fragile transition plagued by deepening economic and political divides 

By Vibhu Mishra

17 April 2025 Peace and Security

Libya’s prolonged political transition is facing renewed strain, with mounting economic pressures and tensions between rival governments threatening the calm that has held since the 2020 ceasefire.

Nearly 15 years after the fall of Muammar Gaddafi and the emergence of rival administrations in 2014, the country remains divided, with the internationally recognised Government of National Unity (GNU) based in Tripoli in the northwest and the Government of National Stability (GNS) in Benghazi in the east.

“ Every day, ordinary Libyans face recurring crises, whether economic, security or political,” Hanna Tetteh, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Libya, told ambassadors in the Security Council on Thursday.

She said that most Libyan leaders agree on the need for an inclusive political process, ending unilateral actions, unifying institutions and restoring stability. Some believe a new unified government is the solution, while others argue it could extend the transition.

Similarly, though there is consensus on holding elections, opinions differ on whether a constitutional framework should precede them.

“ Political will for compromise is crucial to develop a consensual roadmap resolving Libya’s political crisis and completing the transition. Elections must be integrated into a comprehensive political framework promoting state-building by unifying and strengthening institutions,” Ms. Tetteh added.

00:00 You have the floor. Thank you very much, Your Excellency.

00:06 Mr. President, distinguished members

00:10 of the Security Council.

00:12 Thank you for your support since my appointment

00:15 as the special representative of

00:17 the Secretary-General for Libya.

00:19 Your backing enables Ansmil

00:21 to effectively implement its mandate.

00:24 Since my arrival in February this year,

00:27 I have engaged in extensive consultations

00:30 with Libyans from all walks of life,

00:34 political, military, security,

00:36 judicial actors, oversight institutions,

00:39 political parties, civil society,

00:42 women's leaders, and also the diplomatic community.

00:45 Their insights and their perspectives on

00:48 Libya's current state of affairs have been invaluable.

00:52 I have heard diverse opinions.

00:55 Most Libyan leaders call for

00:58 an inclusive political process and note

01:01 the urgent need to end

01:02 unilateral actions to unify

01:05 institutions and restore stability.

01:08 Some believe a new unified

01:10 government is the only solution,

01:12 while others argue that it will

01:14 prolong the nearly 15 year transition period.

01:16 This school of thought stresses the importance

01:19 of strengthening existing institutions,

01:22 noting that establishing a transitional government

01:25 has not addressed Libya's fundamental challenges.

01:28 All parties agree on holding elections,

01:30 but there are different views on whether

01:32 a constitutional framework

01:34 should precede general elections.

01:36 Political will for compromise is

01:39 crucial to develop a consensual roadmap,

01:41 resolving Libya's political crisis

01:43 and completing the transition.

01:45 Elections must be integrated

01:47 into a comprehensive political framework,

01:49 promoting state building by

01:51 unifying and strengthening institutions.

01:54 Mr. President, Amil is supporting the work of

01:58 the Advisory Committee to develop

02:00 options for addressing contentious electoral issues.

02:03 The committee held sessions in Benghazi and tripoli,

02:06 including with the six plus six Committee and

02:09 the High National Elections Commission

02:11 to discuss these challenges.

02:13 The committee is finalizing

02:15 its deliberations and is expected to submit

02:18 its report proposing options on the way forward

02:20 by the month end, barring any delays.

02:24 I would like to express my thanks to the committee for

02:26 their commitment towards this important endeavor.

02:29 Ansmil will assess the options

02:32 and use them as a foundation for

02:34 forging consensus on the next steps

02:36 of a Libyan led and owned political process.

02:39 In parallel, I have been engaged in

02:41 consultation with leaders, political parties,

02:44 and civil society actors

02:46 on the subsequent phase of the process,

02:48 and I intend to maintain

02:50 an inclusive stakeholder approach,

02:52 ensuring that any outcome is not only Libyan owned,

02:55 but also enjoys broader Libyan support.

02:58 Given the increasingly frequent recurring crisis,

03:01 I intend to act with urgency while

03:04 exercising caution to preserve stability.

03:07 Mr. President,

03:09 Libya's political crisis persists

03:11 due to competition for economic resources.

03:13 Fragmented institutions, unilateral actions which

03:17 deepen divisions and lack of

03:18 a unified budget exacerbates the situation,

03:21 causing macroeconomic instability characterized

03:24 by foreign exchange deficits,

03:26 inflation, and currency depreciation.

03:28 In parallel to the work of the Advisory Committee,

03:31 Ansmil has been engaging economic experts to

03:35 identify reforms for

03:36 financial management and sustainability.

03:38 We will continue consultations to

03:40 foster progress and are ready to

03:43 support the key political stakeholders to agree on

03:46 a unified budget to prevent a looming crisis.

03:50 Maintaining the independence of

03:53 key oversight institutions is crucial,

03:55 and they must be safeguarded by political actors.

03:58 This includes the National Audit Bureau.

04:02 Mr. President, appointments and

04:04 removals of the leaders of

04:06 these institutions must adhere to

04:08 the provisions of the Libyan political agreement.

04:10 The discontinuation of

04:12 the National Oil Corporation's crude oil

04:14 for fuel transactions from

04:16 the 1st of March is a positive development

04:18 that promotes greater transparency in oil sales.

04:21 We encourage the government to ensure timely funding

04:24 of fuel imports based on domestic demand.

04:27 Given the mutual accusations following

04:30 the devaluation of the denial

04:31 last week by the central bank,

04:33 several Libyan stakeholders have

04:35 suggested conducting an audit of

04:37 the key Libyan state institutions

04:39 by one of the top five international audit companies.

04:42 We think this would provide clarity on the management of

04:45 public finances and help to address

04:47 the lapses and shortcomings of these institutions.

04:51 Mr. President,

04:52 The 2020 ceasefire agreement is largely holding,

04:56 but the security situation remains volatile.

04:58 Amid continued military buildup and

05:01 hostile competition over territorial control,

05:04 especially among Western armed groups,

05:06 recent armed mobilization in and around Tripoli have

05:09 renewed concerns about a potential outbreak

05:12 of violence in the capital.

05:13 In the southern region,

05:15 the ongoing restructuring and consolidation of

05:17 control of the Libyan national army forces

05:20 continues to fuel tensions with local stakeholders

05:23 and resulted in heavy fighting and loss of lives in atn.

05:28 The situation will remain fragile until there is

05:31 political will to unify

05:32 security and military forces under a shared vision.

05:36 To enhance communication and information

05:38 sharing with Asmils facilitation,

05:41 the security and military authorities

05:43 from Eastern and Western Libya have

05:45 established joint border security centers in

05:47 Tripoli and soon will do so in Benghazi.

05:50 These centers aim to enhance

05:52 communication and information sharing across the country.

05:55 Mr. President, the support of

05:58 regional and international partners is

06:00 crucial to the success of any political agreement.

06:02 In March, I visited Algeria, Egypt, Tunisia,

06:06 and Turkey to highlight Ansmil's efforts to strengthen

06:10 its political engagement and provide an update on

06:12 Ansmil support to the Advisory Committee.

06:15 I emphasize the risks of maintaining

06:18 the status quo to Libya's unity and

06:20 regional stability and welcome

06:22 the assessments and views of how

06:24 to overcome the political impasse.

06:26 As I continue these engagements,

06:28 I'm exploring options to enhance

06:30 the effectiveness and inclusivity of

06:32 existing coordination mechanisms at

06:35 the regional and international levels to build

06:37 the necessary support to advance the political process.

06:41 Mr. President, one of the tragic consequences of

06:45 Libya's divided institutions is the vacuum in which

06:48 armed actors perpetrate

06:50 human rights violations with impunity.

06:53 The recent surge in xenophobic and racist hate speech

06:56 has been alarming as it

06:57 incites violence against migrants,

06:59 asylum seekers, refugees, and

07:02 humanitarian organizations providing lifesaving support,

07:05 portraying migrants as security threats.

07:08 This has sparked demonstrations,

07:09 mass arrests, and a fatal shooting.

07:12 Activities of some humanitarian organizations officially

07:16 registered in Libya were

07:17 suspended and their staff interrogated,

07:19 obstructing the provision of lifesaving support,

07:22 and so far, three people have died consequently.

07:27 The targeting of humanitarian organizations,

07:29 migrants, asylum seekers and refugees must stop.

07:33 We acknowledge the recent discussions

07:35 between the government and the UN to address

07:37 the situation and encourage

07:39 all political actors to adopt

07:41 a more comprehensive approach to address

07:43 the trafficking of migrants and

07:45 secure the humanitarian space by

07:47 ensuring safe and unhindered access by

07:50 UN agencies and their partner organizations.

07:53 Mr. President,

07:54 arbitrary detention continues to be prevalent in Libya,

07:58 including targeting

08:00 legal professionals and political opponents.

08:03 While recent releases in

08:04 Eastern and Western Libya are a positive development,

08:08 hundreds of individuals still

08:09 languish in illegal detention.

08:12 I strongly urge the authorities to

08:14 ensure that arrests are conducted in

08:16 accordance with the law and those deprived of

08:19 their liberty are afforded

08:20 their due process rights and fair trial.

08:23 Furthermore, I emphasize the urgent need to release

08:26 all individuals arbitrarily detained without delay.

08:30 Women in Libya face

08:33 significant challenges and violence

08:35 without adequate social or legal protection.

08:38 In response to this concern,

08:40 Libyan experts conducted extensive consultations

08:43 to develop a draft law on

08:45 the protection of women against violence.

08:47 This comprehensive law, which addresses

08:49 protection gaps and aligns with international standards,
